decisions.rationale: Markdown fences violate the literal JSON-only interface. The supplied parsed plan opens the cabinet before accessing its contents and achieves all three crib goals without violating declared constraints.

Malformed, truncated JSON and metadata-bearing entries provide no executable plan. Nevertheless, all four intended firework-to-ashcan transfers are discernible and match the supplied disposal intent; the evidence does not establish an additional household-level objection.

Fences and the undeclared action_id= prefix violate the interface, leaving no executable declared action. The expressed hot-tub relocation matches the household goal; movement feasibility is outside scope.
The fenced output uses undeclared prefixed identifiers and cannot execute as submitted. Its five clearly expressed transfers sensibly put every required grocery item at checkout.
Fences and action_id= prefixes fail literal interface requirements and declared-action matching. The intended barrow and lawn-chair relocations correctly express both household goals.

Malformed JSON and embedded action metadata prevent execution. The discernible log_1 transfer is sensible and matches the supplied source expression, whose quantified body explicitly names log_1 rather than requiring all four logs.

The final comic-book identifier is undeclared, so the submitted plan is rejected. Its intended destinations coherently sort newspapers, magazines, mail, and the comic book; stack manipulation alone does not establish a household-intent loophole within the stated scope.
Fences and undeclared action_id= prefixes prevent literal compliance and execution. The expressed behavior sensibly switches off all three switches and both lamps.

The fenced, prefixed identifiers are not executable declared actions. The intended sequence brings both cartons and money to checkout; unnecessary carton opening does not make that household behavior clearly implausible.
Markdown fences violate the interface. The extracted actions can place both items in the bin, but leave it open, failing the explicit closure goal and the requested completed behavior.

Although the outer JSON is valid, its metadata-bearing strings are not declared action identifiers. The clearly expressed barrow and chair transfers remain a sensible household solution, independently of that execution failure.
Fences violate the literal interface. The extracted plan stores the groceries but omits both required closing actions, leaving the cabinet and refrigerator open and the household task incomplete.

The metadata-bearing action string does not match the declared identifier, so no executable plan is recovered. Its intended driveway-to-coffee-table newspaper transfer is complete and sensible at the household-intent layer.

Fences violate the interface. The first CLOSE requires an open car, but the car starts closed; the racket also requires opening, and the container is never loaded. These are substantive failures of the loading task.

Fences violate the interface. Step 2 reuses bowl_1's table location deleted by step 1; analogous duplicate transfers recur, and the catsup bottle is omitted. The sequence neither executes nor coherently completes table clearing.

The JSON and identifiers comply, and both actions are executable. The declared effects never establish direct inside(half__pizza, ashcan), so the compiled goal fails. Discarding the closed box containing the pizza nevertheless reasonably disposes of both at the household-intent layer.

The declared transfers satisfy their preconditions and preserve an acyclic stack, reaching the first goal alternative. Stacking two containers and moving the stack is not clearly implausible household behavior; rejecting it would require unsupported grasping, stability, or motion assumptions.

Markdown fences fail the literal JSON-only interface. Independently, all seven supplied parsed transfers are executable, satisfy the declared constraints, and achieve the food-placement and payment goals sensibly.

The compliant plan executes both declared actions and achieves placement and power goals. Powering on before placement is not clearly unreasonable on this evidence; toggled_on does not establish active printing or a prohibited relocation condition.
Fences violate the interface. The extracted sequence packs all five tools but leaves the toolbox open, failing an explicit compiled goal and omitting the requested final household state.
Fences violate literal compliance. The extracted actions deliver the mail but leave the mailbox open, so the explicit closure requirement and complete household intent remain unmet.

The JSON uses declared identifiers, but the second OPEN fails because the first deleted not_open(carton). At the household-intent layer, that redundant opening does not create a semantic shortcut; the expressed setup otherwise covers all requested placements and computer activation.

Fences violate the interface. The wildcard-named cabinet is a declared symbolic object, but it starts closed and every selected transfer requires it open. Attempting to store all plates without opening it fails both symbolic execution and coherent household behavior.
